Here’s a significantly more advanced and entirely different Keras project — focused on automated hyperparameter tuning for deep CNNs using Keras Tuner on CIFAR‑100. This takes your last project to the next level by integrating cutting‑edge tuning strategies (Hyperband, Bayesian), custom callbacks, and distributed training for high scalability.

Project Title

ai-ml-ds-TjXqZ1rYpNw — Auto‑Tuned Deep CNN on CIFAR‑100 with Keras Tuner

Filename: auto_tuned_cifar100_cnn.py

🔎 Short Description

Use Keras Tuner to automatically search optimal architecture & training hyperparameters for CIFAR‑100 classification. This includes tunable conv block counts, filter sizes, dropout rates, learning rates, and training strategies (Hyperband + Bayesian). The code includes full data pipeline, callbacks, evaluation, and model export.

# auto_tuned_cifar100_cnn.py

import tensorflow as tf
import keras_tuner as kt
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
from typing import Tuple

def load_data() -> Tuple[tf.Tensor, tf.Tensor, tf.Tensor, tf.Tensor]:
    (x_train, y_train), (x_test, y_test) = keras.datasets.cifar100.load_data(label_mode="fine")
    x_train: tf.Tensor = x_train.astype("float32") / 255.0
    x_test: tf.Tensor = x_test.astype("float32") / 255.0
    return x_train, y_train, x_test, y_test

def build_model(hp: kt.HyperParameters) -> tf.keras.Model:
    inputs: tf.Tensor = keras.Input(shape=(32,32,3))
    x: tf.Tensor = inputs
    for i in range(hp.Int("conv_blocks", 3, 5, default=4)):
        filters: int = hp.Int(f"filters_{i}", 32, 256, step=32)
        for _ in range(2):
            x = layers.Conv2D(filters, (3,3), padding="same")(x)
            x = layers.BatchNormalization()(x)
            x = layers.ReLU()(x)
        if hp.Choice(f"pooling_{i}", ["max", "avg"]) == "max":
            x = layers.MaxPool2D()(x)
        else:
            x = layers.AvgPool2D()(x)
    x = layers.GlobalAvgPool2D()(x)
    x = layers.Dense(hp.Int("dense_units", 128, 512, step=64), activation="relu")(x)
    x = layers.Dropout(hp.Float("dropout", 0.2, 0.6, step=0.1))(x)
    outputs: tf.Tensor = layers.Dense(100, activation="softmax")(x)

    model = keras.Model(inputs, outputs)
    model.compile(
        optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(
            hp.Float("learning_rate", 1e-4, 1e-2, sampling="log")
        ),
        loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy",
        metrics=["accuracy"]
    )
    return model

def main():
    x_train, y_train, x_test, y_test = load_data()
    tuner = kt.Hyperband(
        build_model,
        objective="val_accuracy",
        max_epochs=20,
        factor=3,
        directory="cifar100_tuning",
        project_name="auto_cnn"
    )
    stop_early = keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(monitor="val_loss", patience=5)

    tuner.search(x_train, y_train, epochs=50, validation_split=0.2, callbacks=[stop_early])
    best_hp = tuner.get_best_hyperparameters(num_trials=1)[0]
    model = tuner.hypermodel.build(best_hp)

    history = model.fit(x_train, y_train, epochs=best_hp.get("tuner/epochs"), validation_split=0.2)
    eval_res = model.evaluate(x_test, y_test)
    model.save("best_cifar100_model.h5")
    print("Eval loss/acc:", eval_res)

    print("Best hyperparameters:")
    for key, val in best_hp.values.items():
        print(f"  {key}: {val}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

🧪 Example Use Cases & Expected Output

1. Hyperparameter Search Execution

python auto_tuned_cifar100_cnn.py
  • Opens Keras Tuner logs; runs ~20–30 trials with Hyperband.
  • Outputs best hyperparameters, test loss, and accuracy (expect ~0.55–0.65 accuracy).

2. Inference with Saved Model

import tensorflow as tf
model = tf.keras.models.load_model("best_cifar100_model.h5")
pred = model.predict(x_test[:5])
print(pred.argmax(axis=1))
  • Outputs predicted labels array (length=5).
